title: Shell Impact
summary: An allied kinetic shell striking the isometric ground, painted: a burst of white-gold petal strokes and a tiny hot core at the contact, a fan of dry-brush dirt thrown straight up, hot white-gold spark comets shooting up in a narrow cone on gravity arcs, a few dirt flicks tumbling out and landing, and steel-and-dust billows (each a dry-brush dab with shadow, body and lit top) born one after another that bloom fast, drag to a stop and rise into a leaning column as they thin. Under it a separate squashed ground pass: ink-splatter sprays flung out evenly all round, low dust rolling along the floor, grit skidding out and a scuff splat that fades. Motion is physical (stagger, drag, gravity, buoyancy), so nothing moves in lockstep. Kinetic, not plasma: no crackle, no shock hoop, warm only on the flash and sparks, so the body reads cool and a crowd of 8-20 hits stays a scatter of small splashes. About 300 ms at 60 fps, 512 px cells drawn at 64 px; the ground scuff's long axis is about 44-48 px.

grid.order: row-major: frame 0 top-left, left to right, then top to bottom
row-major: frame 0 top-left, left to right, then top to bottom

integration: Two sprites, one impact node at the shell's ground contact. Draw order: scuff, then puff. Shared pivot at canvas (0.5, 0.60); drawn at 64 px that is ~6 px below the sprite centre.
Scuff sheet is already projected (view_squash 0.42); do not squash it again. Puff sheet stays full height.

Play once, 60 fps, 18 unique frames, 6x3 atlases, 300 ms. Additive for both; scuff also exports a multiply holdout for light floors. Painted at 512 px per cell, drawn at 64 px. The scuff peaks at ~44 px wide x ~17 px deep (64 px cell) around 150 ms.
Many at once: 8-20 hits may overlap. No per-hit screen shake or flash; any shake is a game-side salvo decision.
Persistent craters, if wanted, are a separate game-side decal; the scuff splat fades with the sheet and leaves nothing on the floor.
Shell flight, damage and fire rate are unset; 64 px cell / ~48 px long axis / 300 ms is the presentation contract until the RTS sim exists.
